title: integration-turnstile-weeknote-2028-12-29
body:
Turnstile weekly sync — 2028-12-29

Attendees: Marisol (owner), Ethan, Priya, Jonah, Sam, plus SE liaisons from Atlas Retail and Nightingale Labs (brief join).

Meeting snapshot (quick bullets):
- Focus: unblock three active integrations, validate canary behavior for model-pin change, and confirm private deployment readiness for PraxisAI.
- Tone: tactical; mix of customer escalations and infra follow-ups.

1) Atlas Retail — status: yellow (customer-facing outage window last Saturday)
- Symptom: intermittent webhook delivery failures causing order sync lag (errors: 401 signature mismatch followed by 429 on retries).
- Root cause hypothesis: misaligned timestamp tolerance between Atlas signature library and our gateway signing. Atlas updated SDK last week; their library now includes millisecond precision.
- Recent actions: Ethan verified gateway signature verifier patch (runtime: accept ±500ms and millisecond granularity) — patch merged to staging (PR 487). Atlas applied SDK fix in their test environment.
- Metric: peak backlog reduced from 6k to 900 events after staggered retry policy rolled out on Saturday; tail latency unchanged.
- Blocker: production rollout requires a small gateway config change that needs compliance review because it touches auth code. Compliance impact tracked in PROSERV-842.
- Temporary mitigation: switched Atlas to our webhook proxy (non-prod) to smooth ingestion while compliance completes review.
- Owner / ETA: Ethan to coordinate compliance checklist with Legal by 2029-01-03; Prod deploy targeted 2029-01-07 if green.

2) Nightingale Labs — status: green with a performance caveat
- Focus: model pinning + quantization testing for their clinical summarization pipeline. They need deterministic output for audit logs.
- Finding: 16-bit quantized variant gives same semantic outputs on 95% eval prompts but changes tokenization boundaries for three template prompts (regression risk).
- Action: Priya ran the eval suite and created a small shim that enforces original tokenization for the three templates; shim increases per-request CPU overhead by ~12ms.
- Operational note: Canary rollout at 5% traffic started Tuesday; observed 3% increase in average token cost due to longer prefixes and shim overhead. Cost is acceptable under their committed usage tier.
- Blocker: Nightingale asks for SLA language confirming deterministic pin behavior under quantized fallbacks — legal draft needed.
- Owner / ETA: Priya to produce canary metrics snapshot and draft SLA addendum for legal review by 2028-12-31.

3) PraxisAI — status: red (data residency gating private deploy)
- Need: private deployment in EU region with customer-managed KMS and HSM integration for key wrapping. PraxisAI also requires additional audit log retention (3 years).
- Observations: our private control plane supports KMS integration but HSM handoff steps are still manual and require an infra runbook update. Audit log retention longer than 90 days currently requires enterprise add-on config changes.
- Mitigations: Jonah started a runbook draft for HSM onboarding (linked in Confluence). Sam validated the KMS plugin handshake in a lab with simulated keys; handshake passed but rotated-key rekey scenario failed.
- Blocker: Security sign-off pending on rekey handling; this is on the critical path for Praxis acceptance testing.
- Owner / ETA: Jonah + Sam to complete rekey test matrix by 2029-01-05; target security re-review 2029-01-08.

Operational items (platform-facing)
- KV cache warmup experiment: ran a 24h warmup script for Atlas workloads; cache hit improved from 18% to 46% on prefixes under 64 tokens. Resulted in ~8% reduction in tail latency (95th percentile). Note: warmup uses ~120GB of cached KV (temp).
- Batching config tweak: lowered max-batch-wait from 12ms to 8ms for low-latency routes; saw p50 improve by 6ms but throughput drop on small-burst windows — will monitor this week.
- Canary rollout policy update: added automatic rollback threshold at +15% cost delta or +10% quality regression (based on eval suite). Canary relies on shadow traffic capture to evaluate.

Open questions / discussion points for next sync
- Do we standardize millisecond-tolerant signature verifier across all gateway clusters (yes/no)? Costs: small CPU increase vs reduction in webhook friction.
- Should we expose a per-customer 'tokenization-stable' flag to force original tokenizer for a customer on model pin change? (Priya suggests opt-in shim vs platform-level flag).
- How aggressive should KV warmup be for Dedicated pools vs Hosted? Current warmup uses non-trivial memory; needs quota guardrails.

Action items (owner + due date)
- ETHAN: Complete compliance signoff for gateway signature change and schedule prod deploy (2029-01-03).
- PRIYA: Finalize Nightingale canary metrics report and SLA addendum draft (2028-12-31).
- JONAH: Finish HSM runbook and rekey test matrix; hand to Security (2029-01-05).
- SAM: Run extended rekey test with rotated keys and report findings (2029-01-04).
- MARISOL: Collate customer-facing one-pager for Atlas outage postmortem and share with CS (2029-01-02).

Notes to self / informal: 
- Quick check: add a short checklist to PR 487 to remind reviewers about timestamp edge cases and integration tests that mock millisecond timestamps.
- Slack threads: keep #se-turnstile-alerts pinned for Prod outages; move non-urgent convo to #se-turnstile-discuss.
- Retrospective: schedule a 30min retrospective on Jan 10 to review webhook changes and warmup memory usage with infra + cost team.

Next sync: weekly cadence maintained; next meeting 2029-01-05 10:00 PT. Agenda: compliance status (Atlas), HSM rekey signoff (PraxisAI), canary metrics review (Nightingale).

End of note.

(Informal draft — will update post-action completions)
